releases.name: reeve 0.4.1
releases.body:
**The pilot pain fixes land, and steps can hand data to each other.** The
v4.3 round (plan `next-round-plan-v4.md`) ships five workstreams on top of
the 0.4.0 engine:

- **Real done criteria (P1.1)**: a v2 step only counts as done when the host
  context shows an idle convergence entry after the last assistant text
  (P1.0 measurement, `evidence/m4/`) — mid-run narration no longer
  masquerades as a terminal state, and running steps are never re-dispatched
  (waiting is the cost of judging "running", never repeated side effects).
- **Declared-step output validation (P1.2)**: `step.schema` is now wired —
  replies are validated through `validateValue` in the `pollAll` done branch
  before the running→done move — and `step.outputs` must exist on disk as
  files (`~/` is expanded by the engine through an injected fs face,
  `fs-face.js`). Only schema/outputs failures are retryable (fixed cooldown,
  default 30s; no exponential backoff — subagent costs are minutes, not
  milliseconds); steps in `pendingRetry` are non-terminal so a run cannot
  close while a leaf step cools down, and a circuit-breaker close during
  cooldown reports `consecutive-failures` with the pending step marked
  `retry-pending`. Journal records gain a `version: 1` field (old records
  without it still load, with a warn).
- **Step data plane, phase 1 (R)**: steps with a schema persist structured
  output in the journal (`payload.output`, 32 KiB write cap →
  `output-over-limit`, non-retryable). Downstream prompts reference it with
  `{{outputs.<stepId>}}` or `{{outputs.<stepId>.<key>}}` — strict two-form
  lexer (no whitespace tolerance, dotted stepIds rejected at the source,
  literal `{{` is a compile error), three compile-time reference checks
  (exists / within the deps transitive closure / has a schema) with
  Did-you-mean candidates, render-time 32 KiB injection cap
  (`injection-over-limit`, non-retryable; rendered prompts are exempt from
  the 8000-char schema cap by design), and `renderPrompt` exported as a pure
  function (the future `dry_run` consumer). Amend fingerprints gain a third
  dimension — an imported downstream requires all referenced upstreams
  imported with their old outputs recoverable, and an upstream change
  cascades along reference closures (non-referencing steps keep the old
  per-step semantics). Hole handoffs that would strand referenced upstreams
  under done downstreams are rejected (fail-closed).
- **lightflow absorption (Q)**: unknown stepId references suggest the
  nearest candidate by edit distance (threshold `max(2, ⌈len/2⌉)`; Q1);
  escalation answers carry a `source` (`harness`/`api`/`panel`, `unknown`
  for legacy shapes) and `answerFor` accepts the legacy bare string again
  (Q3); salvage gains a machine-readable `runStatusCode` six-code mapping
  (0 completed / 1 failed / 2 blocked-escalation / 3 interrupted /
  4 journal-torn / 5 unknown) with a `--status <journalPath>` CLI entry that
  exits with the code (Q4); declarations accept `description` and
  `metadata` labels (Q5; `secret_keys` deliberately not provided).
- **Patch context (P3)**: `buildPatchContext({ storage, runId, scriptPath })`
  is a library-level export returning the failure point (reason/site/
  bodyOffset), completed asks, and the base script fingerprint, so a host
  caller can compose a patch; `registerSession` carries `baseExecution`
  into review context. The host-side caller is still missing and declared as
  such.
- **TypeScript script front-end (P4)**: `.ts` workflow scripts are stripped
  type-only via esbuild 0.28.2 (new plugin dependency) and fed to the same
  vm sandbox through a byte-identical wrapper (`script-wrap.js`, single
  source of truth shared with the JS path); the sole coordinate system is
  the .ts source text, captured before transform; a missing esbuild platform
  package fails with an explicit error. The JS path is untouched.

SKILL.md write-backs cover all of the above (§6 report contract, §9 done
semantics, §11 outputs/

releases.name: reeve 0.4.0
releases.body:
**The orchestration engine ships: declarative runs, sandboxed workflow
scripts, and the plan-gate review loop, all in one plugin.** reeve stops being
"provider gate + review skill" and becomes a dynamic-workflow host: long
multi-step jobs run as real engine runs with a journal, a salvage path when
they fail, and a code-enforced review gate before any plan/script executes.

- **Declarative runs** (`plugin/src/engine/`): jobs are pure-data declarations
  (`runId` + `steps[{stepId, prompt, deps, schema?, ...}]`, validated by
  `declaration.schema.json`); the scheduler dispatches ready steps concurrently
  (deps are the only control flow), every transition lands in an on-disk
  journal, and failed/interrupted runs still produce a salvage report (all ask
  results, the failure point, a mermaid graph with a red tail) rendered from
  the journal alone.
- **Production session driver** (`driver-session.js`): steps run as real host
  sessions (`create` → `wait` → `context`, timeouts, interrupts) — no mocks.
- **Workflow scripts** (`script-runner.js`): a bare ESM function body wrapped
  as `async function main(F){…}` and executed in a whitelisted vm sandbox
  (deterministic by construction — no `Date`/`Math.random`/`fetch`/timers;
  violations fail closed). The facade exposes six members: `ask` (schema
  validation with a 3-attempt repair loop), `run` (literal commands, statically
  scanned into review), `phase`, `hole`/`escalate` (suspend-for-answer), `log`.
- **Resume with prefix import**: reruns replay finished asks from the journal
  when the call-site position, prompt hash and prefix hash all match (v2
  call-site matching — edit the tail, keep the prefix; edit the head, rerun
  from there). Side effects are never cached: "zero ask reruns" does not mean
  "zero side-effect re-execution".
- **Script patching** (`script-patch.js`): mechanical post-failure amendment —
  `applyPatch` writes the patched file alongside the untouched base, journals a
  `patch` event (base→patched fingerprints, anchor, call-seq position), and the
  rerun classifies failures inside the patched segment as `patch-failed`.
- **Plan gate** (`plan-gate.js`, `review_gate` tool): plans, engine-run
  declarations and workflow scripts register with the gate; verdicts from
  review sessions bind to the exact file bytes (round 1 can open the gate,
  changing a byte closes it again — fail-closed); root-session-only
  registration; human override stays a separate face. Decision behavior is
  pinned by a 26-row decision matrix fixture.
- **Creation skill ships in-pack**: `skills/declarative-workflows/` is the
  full authoring contract for both frontends (script path + declarative path),
  translated/adapted from ZCode's bundled `dynamic-workflows` skill
  (Apache-2.0; attribution in the skill's `THIRD-PARTY.md`), kept byte-identical
  with the OpenCodeConfig sync copy.
- **Panel** (`extensions/reeve`): run ledger with four-state step cards (一眼
  可辨 done/running/failed/blocked), a DAG view (declarations render
  steps+deps as mermaid; scripts render phase timelines), and approval cards
  showing script summary, scanned command literals and phase lists. The
  deterministic audit harness grows to 51 checks across locales and dark mode.
- `provision.json`: version 0.4.0, `enginePlugin.spec` realigned (it had
  drifted back to 0.3.0).

releases.name: reeve 0.3.0
releases.body:
**The review skill now ships every upstream rule doc (7 → 64), not a hand-picked
subset.** The previous snapshot was pinned at `alibaba/open-code-review` v1.13.1
with 7 rubrics chosen by language. Re-checking today: upstream is at **v1.13.8**
(64 docs, 324,004 bytes) and our 7 files are byte-identical to that tag, as is
the `Category`/`Severity` enum file — so the snapshot was stable, but the
selection was not: it missed the **domain** rules (`github_workflows.md`,
`github_config.md`) that cover the 9 workflows and 4 `.github` configs in
reeve + ocrc, and `yaml.md` was only 86 bytes ("check key spelling").

- `skills/review/` now carries all 64 upstream rule docs as verbatim copies,
  plus `UPSTREAM.sha256` (per-file hash pinned to a commit, not a tag).
- New `skills/review/review-map.json`: extension → rule selection table
  (REEVE-authored; upstream's internal mapping was never copied). The table in
  `SKILL.md` is **generated** from it, not hand-maintained.
- New `scripts/check-review-map.mjs`: `--write` regenerates the table,
  `--check` fails when the table is stale, a rubric is unlisted, two rules claim
  the same glob, or the representative path cases resolve to the wrong file.
- `scripts/check-plugin-pack.mjs` now also asserts
  `provision.json`'s `enginePlugin.spec === <name>@<version>`, that the packed
  rubric set matches `UPSTREAM.sha256` byte-for-byte, that
  `skills/review/` has no subdirectories, and accepts `--pkg-dir` so negative
  tests run against a throwaway copy.
- New `.gitattributes` pins `plugin/skills/review/*.md` (and the hash manifest)
  to LF; without it a Windows checkout rewrites line endings and the sha256
  gate fails on every Windows CI leg.
- `provision.json`: version 0.3.0, `enginePlugin.spec` caught up from 0.2.8
  (it had drifted since 0.2.9), `enginePlugin.entry` corrected to the real
  unpack layout (`.../components/reeve/package`).
- Notices updated: `NOTICE.md` and the in-package `THIRD-PARTY.md` both list
  all 64 files; upstream verified to have no `NOTICE` file of its own.

releases.name: reeve 0.2.12
releases.body:
**Contract-only release.** Adds `pluginOptions` (`agents.hideBuiltins=false`)
to `provision.json` so ocrc-driven peer installs register the plugin as an
object entry carrying the option — 0.2.11 shipped the feature but left the
contract field out, so peers kept the plain-string entry and native agents
stayed hidden there. No code changes.

releases.name: reeve 0.2.11
releases.body:
**Native agents can stay visible; foreman gets a shape-based fast lane.**

- New plugin option `agents.hideBuiltins` (default `true`, current behavior):
  when `false`, the engine's native `build` / `plan` / `general` / `explore`
  agents keep their config visibility and appear in the composer picker.
  Direct small tasks can then run on the native single-agent path (1× token
  cost) while foreman keeps handling orchestrated ones — the manual mode
  switch that every mainstream coding agent converged on, backed by the
  multi-agent overhead data (Anthropic's research system reports ~15× token
  usage vs a chat) and the SWE-bench gold-patch distribution (median 1–2
  files touched).
- `agents/foreman.md` dispatch judgment rewritten from task **type** to task
  **shape**: three questions (parallelizable subtasks? needs a boundary-locking
  doc? needs independent review?). All "no" → fast lane: one-sentence task
  straight to `executor`, personal verification, **no** planner/critic/reviewer;
  any "yes" → full pipeline. The old dispatch-gate ceremony (written
  justification required to skip planning) is retired — it made the 1–2-file
  majority of real work pay the orchestration tax by default. The ≤3-file
  hint is a calibration default, to be revisited against real dispatch
  ledger data, not a law.
